newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt share prices rise despite minor profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Egypt share prices rise despite minor profit-taking.

text.p: Milling and cement firms continued to propel Egyptian share prices higher on Sunday despite profit-taking in some stocks, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index rose 3.9 points to 276.17 points on turnover of 25.80 million pounds ($7.59 million).
The index has been steadily climbing to record highs since it broke last week the previous record of 255.05 points set in October 1994.
"The market is changing before us. Everything's on the rise and there is a lot of foreign demand," said Hany Sayed of El Rashad Securities Brokerage.
Two transactions worth more than 2.25 million pounds in rarely-traded Misr Exterior Bank buoyed turnover and increased share prices 19.00 pounds to 750.00.
Brokers said state-owned Banque Misr was selling part of its stake in the bank to a group of private investors.
Millers were still the most traded firms in the market but some of these popular stocks have been hit by profit-taking, brokers said.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills North Cairo Flour Mills rose 0.10 pounds to 90.00 and Upper Egypt Flour Mills also gained 0.05 to 73.00.
These gains spilled over onto General Silos and Storage which rose 1.55 pounds to 52.30 pounds.
But North Cairo Flour Mills was among the day's top losers, shedding 2.00 pounds to 135.00 pounds. Central Egypt Flour Mills also ended 0.23 pounds down at 46.77.
"Prices have become attractive to sell and there are many other stocks to invest in," Sayed said.
Helwan Portland Cement rose 0.15 pounds to 64.90 in trading spurred by an announcement that the state had relinquished its majority stake in the firm.
The official Holding Company for Mining and Refractories sold investors 22.3 percent of the firm, bringing the total privatised to 52.1 percent.
"International and local funds bought a large tranche as did local investors," said a source close to the deal.
Foreign interest in Egypt's sole cigarette maker Eastern Company pushed share prices 2.25 pounds to 61.00 pounds. Brokers said American cigarette firms were buying stakes in the company.
Of a total 60 stocks traded, 29 rose, 11 fell and the rest closed unchanged.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 430.6 points from Thursday's 419.9 points and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also gained 1.43 points to 190.1.
